Sandbagging by a password-locked model could potentially be uncovered by estimating the capability scaling of the algorithm through small experiments using known data sets. This approach could allow for the detection of sandbagging attempts by revealing discrepancies in the expected capabilities of the model. Additionally, having skilled humans with full information access could help catch such an attack if they had the time and resources to extensively test the provided algorithm on known uncorrupted data sets, which might help in understanding the true capability curve of the algorithm.

Standard capability elicitation might fail to reveal the sandbagging because the password locking of the model could be so effective that there are no hints of the dangerous capabilities. If the model's capabilities are effectively hidden, then the usual methods of eliciting capabilities based on observable signals may not work, as there would be no signals to boost or detect. Thus, without a clear understanding of how the model is actually functioning, efforts to uncover hidden capabilities may be unsuccessful.
